Aisha Khan: Quick thread to align on pilot design: AcmePay & Lighthouse asked for lower steady cost but firm p99 during spikes. We need a concrete approach for Q3 pilots. Proposals: 1) slice dedicated pool into 'steady + burst tokens' 2) predictive prewarm process 3) tiered fallback to quantized variant. Which combination?
Tom Rivera: Slicing + tokens seems promising. Tokens are consumed when usage > steady baseline; tokens expire after window. Keeps steady cost low for tenants who don't spike.
Ellen Park: UX ask from CS: tenants must see token balance and prediction-based warnings in Console. Also a way to convert tokens to committed headroom if they want.
Diego Morales: Runtime concerns: token enforcement requires admission gate at scheduler + fast admission path. Predictive prewarm requires short lead-time model load; for 13B models that's ~35-60s unless we keep minimal warmed replicas.
Nikhil Desai: Finance: tokens = prepaid credits billed monthly. If we expose carryover, it needs a cap. Prefer 0-10% carryover or a 48h auto-expiry window.
Aisha Khan: Operational risk: long carryover + aggressive prewarm might create steady spike patterns that defeat autoscale. We should prototype attack scenarios.
Tom Rivera: Agree. Also think about session affinity: steering sessions to warmed replicas reduces variance. Could be part of the SDK/route config.
Ellen Park: Pilot launch checklist suggestion:
- baseline telemetry ingest (RPS, queue depth, latency p50/p95/p99)
- token accounting and billing simulation
- Console token panel + alerts
- SLA wording for pilot (target p99, escalation)
Diego Morales: For admission control ordering: propose priority: dedicated steady -> token-backed burst -> shared spot -> quantized fallback. That gives predictable ordering and graceful degradation.
Nikhil Desai: Billing rule sketch (for simulation):
```
monthly_bill = committed_fee + max(0, token_used - included_tokens)*token_price
```
Cap token liability per tenant = committed_fee * 0.25 (configurable).
Tom Rivera: On autoscale policy, recommend two-layer approach: fast prewarm scaler (predictive, uses short-term forecast), and slower cluster autoscaler (reactive, uses observed queue). Config example:
```
fast_scaler: lookahead_seconds=90, target_util=0.7
cluster_scaler: cool_down=300s, target_util=0.6
```
This reduces oscillation and gives lead-time for model load.
Aisha Khan: Questions for pilot scope decision: a) do we require tenants to opt-in to token model? b) do we allow cross-tenant pooling during pilot? c) how do we measure success?
Ellen Park: a) yes opt-in. b) no cross-tenant pooling for pilot (keeps billing and risk isolated). c) success metrics: p99 latency adherence, token utilization vs predicted, pilot NPS from CS.
Diego Morales: Implementation owners: scheduler + admission (Tom), prewarm service + warm replica bookkeeping (Diego), console token UI + UX (Ellen), finance sim + pricing knobs (Nikhil), product docs + SLA (Aisha).
Aisha Khan: I'll draft a one-pager w/ metrics and a minimal SLA. Let's run sims before committing to carryover policy. Can ops-bot create ticket for infra sims?
ops-bot: Created ISSUE-4729 "pilot: token-backed burst sims + predictive-prewarm prototype" assigned to @Tom, @Diego.
Aisha Khan: Great. Please bring sim results and a pricing sensitivity table to Wed sync. :rocket:
